posts.author: LilyiacGaming01
posts.body:
Hey, I am trying to make my own tilesets by copy and paste from existing tilesets that comes with RPG Maker MV.
My problem is that rpg maker's original tilesets everything is so close together in the file without interfering with each other.
Also, is this allowed? I wanted to use other tilesets for my game from other creators, but lost track quick over the credits, so I rather make my own versions of the ones already existing in MV.
This is one of the tilesets that comes with MV. Objects are close but won't interfere with each other.
And then there is mine. If I keep any of these objects closer to each other, they will interfere with each other. f.ex If I want the window with pink curtains open, the window with the pink curtains closed can not be any closer than they are in this picture or else I will get the window I want with parts of the other window I don't want.

posts.author: CoryH
posts.body: Change the grid size to 48x48 and it'll be a lot easier. I usually use the snap to grid setting when I'm moving tiles, that way I know it will not clip into the next tile.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
As for your general problem:
you can have empty space on the tileset, but only if it is part of the tile and design.
Each tile is 48x48 pixel. that is a fixed size and cannot be changed directly and is the reason why in the original tilesets everythig is directly next to each other.
If you want a space around any object, like around the window, then it needs to be part of the tile as in window plus space is exactly 48x48 (or 48x96 for two-tile windows etc).
You do NOT want excessive space between each tile, because that space would come out of the other tiles near or between them - and the RMs have only a limited number of tiles. So wasting tiles on empty space is a no-go.
sometimes you have no choice to do so to make sure the decoration looks correct, like around the thrones in the example tiles - but you should limit that as much as possible.

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
Another thing is resizing tiles to fit in better.
So if you had a Cupboard that was 3 tiles high but 110 Pixels, reduce it to 96 pixels height to make it fit into 2 tiles.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
If you're going to make your own assets, it makes sense to read the instructions about them. You can click Help -> Contents -> Documentation -> Asset Standards.
It gives you the basic information like the 48x48 tile size, and if you do anything on the A sheets certain things are expected to be in specific locations on the sheets.
